skills.name: Data Cloud Connect: Source Connections & Connectors
skills.summary: Choosing and configuring the right connector for a new source system before any ingestion begins.
skills.whenToUse: SOW mentions: connecting a new source system, connector setup, Snowflake/Redshift/SharePoint/Heroku Postgres integration, testing a connection, or browsing source objects/schemas before building a pipeline.
skills.bestPractices: Prefer read-only discovery (connector catalog, existing connections) before proposing new connection creation. Different connector types have fundamentally different credential/parameter shapes - Snowflake uses key-pair auth, SharePoint Unstructured uses clientId/clientSecret/tokenEndpoint with no parameters array, Heroku Postgres/Redshift have their own shapes - never assume one generic credential shape fits all connectors. An empty connection list for a connector type usually means 'enabled but not configured yet', not 'feature unavailable' - don't conclude a capability is missing from an empty list alone. Ingestion API connector setup isn't complete until the object schema has been uploaded (schema-upsert) - creating the connection alone is not sufficient, call this out as a distinct scope line. Some external connectors can be created via API but stream creation immediately after may still require UI-only steps - don't promise a fully API-driven path for every connector type in a SOW.

skills.name: Data Cloud Prepare: Data Streams, DLOs & Ingestion
skills.summary: Choosing the right stream category and ingestion mechanism once a source connection exists.
skills.whenToUse: SOW mentions: data streams, Data Lake Objects (DLOs), ingesting data into Data Cloud, Document AI/unstructured file ingestion, or re-scanning/refreshing ingested data after a source update.
skills.bestPractices: Classify each dataset as Profile (person/entity records, needs a primary key), Engagement (time-based events/interactions, needs a primary key + event time field), or Other (reference/config data, needs a primary key) before designing the stream - this classification drives downstream identity resolution and segment eligibility, and should be an explicit SOW decision, not an afterthought. CRM-backed (Salesforce) streams sync on a platform-managed schedule and are not controlled the same way as custom connector streams - don't assume a uniform refresh model across connector types when estimating cadence. For unstructured/document sources (e.g. SharePoint), first-time setup is often richer via the UI than a minimal API-driven flow - flag this as a likely UI-dependent step rather than assuming full API automation. Ingestion API payloads return HTTP 202 (accepted for processing), which is not the same as records being immediately queryable - don't size real-time expectations off acceptance alone. Validation failures on Ingestion API surface in a separate 'Problem Records' DLO family, not as a synchronous error - plan for a review step.

skills.name: Data Cloud Harmonize: DMOs, Mappings & Identity Resolution
skills.summary: Mapping DLOs to DMOs and designing identity resolution rulesets to build a unified profile.
skills.whenToUse: SOW mentions: Data Model Objects (DMOs), field mappings, identity resolution, unified profiles, universal ID, data graphs, or building a single customer/entity view across multiple sources.
skills.bestPractices: Inspect the source DLO's schema before designing a mapping to a DMO - mapping quality depends on understanding the real source shape first, not just the target. Identity resolution runs are asynchronous - a 'ruleset created' result does not mean matching has completed; verify results after execution rather than assuming immediate completion when estimating a timeline. Unified DMO names are ruleset-specific, not a fixed generic name - don't assume one canonical DMO name applies across different identity resolution configurations in a multi-brand/multi-space scope. If DMO listing works but identity resolution is gated/unavailable, that's a phase-specific permission or provisioning gap, not evidence the whole Data Cloud org is broken - diagnose narrowly rather than escalating scope.

skills.name: Data Cloud Schema Introspection: DLO & DMO Field Discovery
skills.summary: Listing and inspecting DLO/DMO schemas (fields, types, primary keys) via the SSOT REST API.
skills.whenToUse: SOW mentions: needing to inspect existing DLO/DMO field definitions, understand what data structures already exist in an org, or a discovery/audit step before designing new mappings or insights.
skills.bestPractices: DLO names always end in __dll and DMO names always end in __dlm - use this to distinguish the two categories when reviewing an org's existing configuration inventory. Exclude system-managed fields (DataSource__c, cdp_sys_*, KQ_*) when summarizing a schema for a business audience - focus on the custom/business fields the customer actually cares about. Retrieving a specific object's real schema before proposing a mapping or calculated insight avoids proposing a design that doesn't match the actual field set.

skills.name: Data Cloud Segment: Building & Publishing Segments
skills.summary: Creating and publishing audience segments and verifying membership/counts after publish.
skills.whenToUse: SOW mentions: audience segmentation, segment creation, segment publishing, member counts, or troubleshooting segment logic in Data Cloud.
skills.bestPractices: Data Cloud segment SQL is a distinct query language from standard Salesforce SOQL - don't assume SOQL syntax or functions apply when scoping segment logic work. Segment creation can be sensitive to API version - pin to a known-stable version when giving implementation guidance rather than assuming the latest default behaves identically. Publish is asynchronous - a segment 'created' or 'published' response doesn't guarantee membership is final; verify with an explicit count or query afterward rather than assuming success from the initial response when estimating timelines. An empty segment list on a Data Cloud org usually means the module is reachable but nothing has been configured yet, not that segmentation is unavailable.

skills.name: Data Cloud Calculated Insights: Creation & Verification
skills.summary: Creating, running, and verifying calculated insights (aggregated metrics) built on unified profile data.
skills.whenToUse: SOW mentions: calculated insights, lifetime value, aggregated/recurring metrics, or a computed metric derived from Data Cloud data that feeds a segment, dashboard, or activation.
skills.bestPractices: Calculated insight execution is not guaranteed synchronous - verify results with an explicit query (e.g. a COUNT or aggregate SQL check) rather than assuming the run command's quick return means the computation is complete, especially when estimating a delivery timeline. Calculated insight assets have different constraints than segment SQL even though both run on Data Cloud SQL - don't assume identical capabilities or limits between the two asset types when scoping work that touches both.

skills.name: Data Cloud Activate: Activation Targets & Downstream Delivery
skills.summary: Setting up activation targets and pushing segments/insights to downstream systems.
skills.whenToUse: SOW mentions: activating a segment, activation targets, data actions, or pushing Data Cloud audiences/data into an external or downstream system (e.g. Marketing Cloud, an ad platform).
skills.bestPractices: Activation design depends on a healthy, already-published upstream segment or insight - don't scope activation work independently of confirming the upstream audience is actually ready first. Destination/platform configuration (activation targets, data action targets) is typically set up before the activation itself, not after - sequence SOW tasks in that order. Downstream credential and platform-specific constraints (e.g. a specific ad platform's own API limits) often live outside Data Cloud's own configuration surface entirely - flag these as a separate validation concern rather than folding them into the Data Cloud estimate.

skills.name: Data Cloud Query & Search: SQL, Vector Search, Metadata Introspection
skills.summary: Running Data Cloud SQL, vector/hybrid search, and metadata introspection against ingested/unified data.
skills.whenToUse: SOW mentions: querying Data Cloud data directly, vector search, semantic/hybrid search, search indexes, or programmatic metadata/schema introspection of DMOs/DLOs.
skills.bestPractices: Data Cloud SQL is a distinct query language from standard Salesforce SOQL, with different capabilities and syntax (e.g. quoted table names) - don't assume SOQL patterns transfer when scoping query/reporting work. For medium-to-large result sets, prefer paginated or asynchronous query patterns over naive single-shot queries, which can time out or be inefficient at scale - flag this in any SOW involving large exports. Vector and hybrid search depend entirely on a healthy, already-created search index - don't scope a semantic search use case without accounting for search index setup and its own lifecycle as a prerequisite. Hybrid search prefiltering only works on fields explicitly configured as prefilter-capable at index-creation time - this needs to be planned upfront, not added after the fact.

skills.name: Data Cloud Orchestration: Data Spaces, Data Kits & Cross-Phase Design
skills.summary: Deciding how work spans Connect -> Prepare -> Harmonize -> Segment -> Act, and managing data spaces/data kits.
skills.whenToUse: SOW mentions: a multi-step/end-to-end Data Cloud pipeline spanning multiple phases, data spaces (multi-brand/region/business-unit partitioning), data kits, or a need to decide which Data Cloud phase a given requirement actually belongs to.
skills.bestPractices: A single monolithic 'set up Data Cloud' scope item usually decomposes into distinct Connect/Prepare/Harmonize/Segment/Act workstreams with different owners and sequencing - break these out explicitly in a SOW rather than estimating them as one lump task. Data Spaces partition profile unification, insights, and activation by brand/region/business-unit without provisioning a separate org - recommend a single default Data Space for simple/pilot scopes, and multiple Data Spaces only when the SOW genuinely calls out separate brands/regions/business units needing isolated unification or segmentation. Cross-phase troubleshooting root causes are often phase-specific gaps (e.g. one module gated by permissions) rather than a whole-product outage - diagnose the specific failing phase rather than assuming an all-or-nothing platform issue.

skills.name: Data Cloud Code Extensions: Custom Python Transformations
skills.summary: Developing, testing, and deploying custom Python code extensions that read/write DLOs and DMOs on Data Cloud's own compute infrastructure.
skills.whenToUse: SOW mentions: custom/bespoke data transformations that built-in Calculated Insights or standard mappings can't express, custom Python logic against Data Cloud data, or a real-time function-based transform (as opposed to a scheduled batch transform).
skills.bestPractices: Distinguish script-based (batch) from function-based (real-time) code extensions upfront - they have different runtime models and should be scoped as distinct SOW line items, not interchangeably. The deployable unit is the generated payload/ subdirectory, not the project root - a SOW/runbook that treats them as the same path will fail at deploy. Required permissions (DLO/DMO read/write) are derived by scanning the entrypoint file, not declared manually - budget a scan-and-review step before first deploy. Custom code extensions consume Data Cloud compute credits per compute unit (distinct from pipeline/query credits), so cost estimates for this capability should size against the codeExtension rate item, not a data-pipeline rate item. Docker is required for deploy but not for local script development/testing - don't over-scope local dev environment setup.

skills.name: Data Cloud Agentforce Session Analysis (Observability)
skills.summary: Reconstructing a single Agentforce session's full trace from Data Cloud's session data model, for debugging/observability.
skills.whenToUse: SOW mentions: Agentforce session tracing, session-level observability/debugging, or auditing what a specific agent conversation actually did using Data Cloud's session data.
skills.bestPractices: This is a Data-Cloud-only observability capability - it reconstructs what Data Cloud already materialized about a session, and cannot answer real-time availability/latency/SLO questions that require platform telemetry beyond Data Cloud. Scope this as a debugging/audit capability, not a substitute for full application performance monitoring, when a SOW conflates general 'observability' with this specific session-reconstruction feature.

skills.name: SOW Technical Review Framework for Data Cloud Scope
skills.summary: A pre-signature risk/feasibility checklist for any Data Cloud SOW - apply alongside whichever other skills match.
skills.whenToUse: Always apply this whenever the SOW/scope document references Data Cloud, Zero Copy, Data Streams, Data Spaces, Calculated Insights, Identity Resolution, Einstein Prediction Builder, Agentforce, or Salesforce-to-external-source integration - regardless of which other skills also match. This is a review framework, not a single narrow trigger.
skills.bestPractices: Flag these recurring risk areas when present in the SOW, each with a concrete recommendation rather than just an observation: (1) Zero Copy - does it require a specific source-platform edition/federation setup not confirmed in the assumptions, and is there a stated ingestion fallback if prerequisites aren't met? (2) Data Streams/ingestion - does the number of business objects/entities match the stated number of streams/instances (one source can feed many objects = many streams - flag if the SOW's language conflates them), and are refresh cadence/freshness SLAs specified? (3) Data Spaces - is the design right-sized for current scope while still extensible for future phases? (4) Predictive models (Prediction Builder/similar) - is there a stated minimum historical data volume for reliable training, does the model need data on an object type different from where it lands via ingestion (an implied sync step that may be unscoped), and are thresholds/outputs static vs dynamic in a way that should be surfaced to the customer? (5) Agentforce/agent integration - treat this as the highest technical risk regardless of how briefly it's scoped; a one-line bullet covering grounding + actions/topics + write-back usually understates its complexity - flag it for a named integration owner. (6) Assumptions section - scan for blank/incomplete/dropped numbered items and unrealistic data-access/timeline assumptions. (7) Commercial math - reconcile whether per-workstream hours and fees actually sum to the stated total (before and after any discount), and whether billing terms match. Track every stated numeric cap ("up to N objects", "up to 1 instance") precisely - these are where scope disputes originate later. Stay evenhanded about vendor design choices (e.g. single vs. multiple Data Spaces) - frame as a trade-off rather than declaring it wrong, unless it conflicts with a stated platform constraint.
